title: Optimize candidate prompts or demonstrations against an explicit evaluator while separating validation data from the final held-out comparison

source.heading: A small example set rewards luck

questions.prompt:
A team wants a prompt that turns support tickets into SQL queries. A model proposes 30 candidate instructions. Each candidate runs on the same 40 tickets with known correct queries, and code counts the correct outputs. The best candidate scores 38 of 40. The team plans to report "about 95% accuracy" as the expected accuracy on the tickets the product will receive in production.

Explain why 38 of 40 is likely to overstate this winner's accuracy on new tickets, and describe the data that would give a trustworthy estimate of its production accuracy.

rubric.point: Explains that the winner was chosen because it scored highest on those same 40 tickets, so its score includes fit to, or luck on, those particular examples (selection makes the score optimistic).
States that the estimate needs a separate held-out set of tickets that the search never used, and whose results do not guide choosing or revising the prompt. Repeated runs on that set are acceptable.

States that the held-out tickets must be representative of the intended production workload (for example drawn from or shaped like real production tickets), since an unrelated or systematically easier set would not support a production-accuracy estimate.

questions.model: The 38 of 40 is the score that made this candidate win out of 30. Picking the highest score favours whichever candidate happened to suit those 40 tickets, partly through luck on a few of them, so the score is biased upwards as a prediction for other tickets. A trustworthy estimate comes from scoring the chosen prompt on a separate held-out set of tickets that played no part in the search and is not used to pick or revise the prompt. Those tickets must be representative of the production workload, such as a sample of real production tickets, because a set that is unrelated or easier than production would not show production accuracy.

c1.text: the prompt is overfitted to the cases, and shows not 95% accuracy in general, but 95% accuracy over this fixed set. The percentage will bu trustworthly if it will include random production tickets, that wasnt included into ticket sets, if the result will be the same on other random tickets, then it is trustworthy

annotations.quote: the prompt is overfitted to the cases
annotations.note: You identify that the winning prompt is fitted to those particular tickets, which is the core reason the score is optimistic.

annotations.quote: shows not 95% accuracy in general, but 95% accuracy over this fixed set
annotations.note: You correctly separate accuracy on the fixed set from accuracy on new tickets.

annotations.quote: that wasnt included into ticket sets
annotations.note: You require tickets the search never used, which is the held-out requirement.
Sampling real production tickets makes the held-out set representative of the intended workload.

c1.feedback: You covered the overfitting to the fixed set, the need for unseen held-out tickets, and the need for them to come from production.
